decision: The agency ran the repair to a closure at event-052, but two definition-of-done items have no supporting evidence: a provider work result and the landlord's confirmation of completion. Authority for the spend is sound (landlord's own approval of GBP 90 plus VAT at event-018, given after the quote at event-015 and before the go-ahead at event-020), so no new approval is needed and no new work order was raised - raising one would duplicate the job booked at event-027. Within mandate I chased the provider for a legible PDF invoice, completion date and photos, asked the tenant to confirm the window now closes, asked the landlord to confirm completion, recorded the data-quality issues, and raised an office task to reopen the request for final checks (I cannot reopen a closed ticket). The case now waits on three named parties, so it ends as request_info rather than an escalation: nothing here requires a human to decide liability, legal or safety.

facts.statement: Tenant reported on 11 Sept 2025 that the bedroom window at Flat 23, 143 Willowmere Road, Alderwick does not close properly and a hinge is rusted.
No landlord spend cap or standing instruction is available in this environment; the authority relied on is the landlord's own approval in the history.
The landlord agreed to a contractor attending (12 Sept, 10:06) and then approved GBP 90 plus VAT for the hinge (12 Sept, 16:03); the agency instructed the provider to proceed afterwards at 16:38.
Lantern Utilities booked the visit for 30 September 2025 and the slot 10:00-17:00 was confirmed to both tenant and provider on 16 September.
No work result was ever recorded; the agency noted the absence on 2 October and the provider's only reply is 'Attached invoice' on 7 October with the attachment unavailable.
The system asked for landlord confirmation of completion on 7 October; no landlord reply follows in the visible history, and the request was closed 74 minutes later.
Agency emails name the landlord as both 'Grace' and 'Felix', and provider emails are signed 'Jenkins' and 'Mercer' for the same provider.

conflicts.description: The landlord is addressed as 'Grace' in the agency's outgoing emails but the landlord's replies and the agency's later emails use 'Felix'.
conflicts.resolution: The landlord's own replies settle landlord-owned questions, so the approval at event-018 stands regardless of the name used. The name discrepancy is a CRM data-quality item flagged to the office (ACT-5); no name was copied into any party letter.

conflicts.description: Event-052 states all checks were completed, while event-036, event-048 and event-049 show the work result, documents and landlord confirmation were outstanding.
conflicts.resolution: The specific records of missing items beat the general closing status line; the ticket is treated as at final_checks and the office is asked to reopen (ACT-5).

red_flags.description: Closure line claims all checks complete while the work result, photos and landlord confirmation are absent from the record; the invoice attachment is unreadable so the invoiced total is unverified against the approved GBP 90 plus VAT.
red_flags.action_taken: Chased provider for a PDF invoice, completion date and photos (ACT-2); asked landlord to confirm completion (ACT-3); asked tenant to confirm the window closes (ACT-1); office task to reopen (ACT-5).

red_flags.description: Inconsistent party names in the agency's own correspondence: landlord 'Grace' vs 'Felix'; provider contacts 'Jenkins' vs 'Mercer' for Lantern Utilities.
red_flags.action_taken: Recorded in the case note (ACT-4) and referred to the office (ACT-5); no name from a message body was reused in a letter to another party.
